blocking_item1_halt_resume_double_count_.bug: at halt time, the v3-driver-pre-1781 code wrote the checkpoint with DSDWriteCheckpoint(DSDIdx - 1, DSDSummary) -- even though DSDSummary's drops/anomalies/bugs counter for THIS window (DSDIdx) had already been incremented and a halt-checkpoint JSON already written for it. On resume (after a human clears the poison lock), DSDResumeFrom = (DSDIdx-1)+1 = DSDIdx -- the SAME halted window would be re-attempted, double-counting it if it halted again (or silently reprocessing it if, e.g., a code fix changed its outcome).
blocking_item1_halt_resume_double_count_.fix: search/drophunt_sweep_driver_v3.g: both halt branches (Mode A line ~331, Mode B line ~356 after edits) now call DSDWriteCheckpoint(DSDIdx, DSDSummary) -- the halted window IS accounted (summary incremented, full receipt + halt-checkpoint JSON both written), so resume correctly starts at DSDIdx+1.

same_turn_item9_known_gaps_additions.per_m_0_structural_reachability: CORRECTED/REFINED per this pass's item2 fix: per_m=0 entries were structurally unreachable via the OLD normal-pass-only emit path (a 0 anywhere among gcd-eligible m implies either DROP (if it's the only outcome, valid_total=0) or ANOMALY (if some other m has a nonzero count) -- both of which HALT before the old normal-pass emission code ran). AFTER item2's fix (full receipts now ALSO emitted at halt time), per_m=0 entries DO now appear in emitted receipts -- specifically in DROP/ANOMALY-labeled halt receipts (confirmed via the synthetic test: per_m=[0] in the DROP-labeled scratchpad/test_halt_receipt_16437e56512d99ab_synthetic_v1.json). So the corrected statement is: per_m=0 is unreachable in a verdict='PASS' receipt (by the lattice's own definition -- PASS requires lift_m=F1_double_prime, i.e. every gcd-eligible m has per_m>=1), but IS reachable (and, since item2, IS actually emitted) in DROP/ANOMALY-labeled receipts.
same_turn_item9_known_gaps_additions.null_unfired_via_driver_path: CONFIRMED with real data this pass: 0/80 sweep-driver-emitted receipts (as of this cert) contain any null per_m entry, i.e. every window the driver itself has processed so far has F1_prime==F1_double_prime (no gcd-excluded m in its residue class). null per_m entries DO occur, but only via the standalone item4 script against b3_index=5 (fib_K=25), which is NOT among the windows the driver itself has processed in fib_K-ascending order yet (359 total windows, 29/358 have F1_prime>F1_double_prime per drophunt_frozen_node_list_v2, so null WILL eventually appear once the driver's fib_K-ascending traversal reaches one of those 29 -- b3_index=5/fib_K=25 is one of the earliest by fib_K, so this will likely be exercised for real early in the actual 358-window launch).
same_turn_item9_known_gaps_additions.anomaly_structurally_unreachable_210_358: CONFIRMED with real data this pass: 210/358 frozen windows have F1_double_prime=1 (computed via search/certs/drophunt_frozen_node_list_v2_20260829.json). For F1_double_prime=1, lift_m can only be 0 or 1 (there is exactly one gcd-eligible m), so 0<lift_m<F1_double_prime (the ANOMALY condition) is IMPOSSIBLE by integer arithmetic -- only DROP (lift_m=0) or PASS/BUG (lift_m=1, distinguished by mult_set) can occur for those 210 windows. ANOMALY can only occur among the remaining 148/358 windows (F1_double_prime>=2).
